name: Charlie Bilello
zh_summary: @charliebilello details $META Q3 revenues up 26% YoY to a record $64.6 billion, but costs/expenses rose 68% YoY to $51.6 billion including $9.9 billion from a $18.6 billion teen mental health settlement, causing operating income to fall 37% YoY to $13 billion and margins to drop to 20% from 40%.
en_summary: @charliebilello details $META Q3 revenues up 26% YoY to a record $64.6 billion, but costs/expenses rose 68% YoY to $51.6 billion including $9.9 billion from a $18.6 billion teen mental health settlement, causing operating income to fall 37% YoY to $13 billion and margins to drop to 20% from 40%.
text: Meta Q3 revenues increased 26% over the last year to a new record high of $64.6 billion. But costs/expenses rose 68% YoY to a record $51.6 billion ($9.9 billion of this was part of the $18.6 billion settlement related to teen mental health/social media). As a result, income from operations fell 37% YoY to $13 billion. And operating profit margins moved down to 20% from 40% a year ago. $META
orig: Meta Q3 revenues increased 26% over the last year to a new record high of $64.6 billion. But costs/expenses rose 68% YoY to a record $51.6 billion ($9.9 billion of this was part of the $18.6 billion settlement related to teen mental health/social media). As a result, income from operations fell 37% YoY to $13 billion. And operating profit margins moved down to 20% from 40% a year ago. $META

text:
$META just posted negative FCF for the first time in over a decade despite beating revenue estimates by over $1B as AI helped lift ad prices 14%.

That's the kind of cash burn I can get behind when Meta's core business keeps getting stronger and management is investing heavily in its next major growth engine.
